additional_considerations.rationale: Causes posterior heel pain from irritation of the bursae around the Achilles insertion, often from ill-fitting footwear or a Haglund deformity.
Tibial nerve compression at the medial heel causes pain, burning, tingling, or numbness radiating to the plantar heel and sole.
Look for an entrance wound and signs of local infection; the patient may not describe a mechanism of injury.
Usually follows rolling the ankle, with ligament tenderness, laxity, edema, and ecchymosis.

source_issues: Heart rate disagrees: doorway HR 69/minute vs patient-note exam HR 72 beats per minute (e004). Both kept (v004, v006).
Exam lines e006 ('Extremities:') and e012 ('Neuro:') are bare section headers split off by the parser; listed in excluded_exam_ids.
Exam lines e010, e011, and e015 do not state the side; the SP notes and history place the findings on the right foot. Kept as written.
The note HPI says ice, massage, and occasional ibuprofen gave 'limited relief' (added as from_note fact f017); the script says massage and ice make the pain better (p012).

The note FH says the patient denies a family history of rheumatologic disorders, while the father has arthritis (p021, type not given). The family rheumatologic denial was not added as a patient fact.

Gold rank 1 lists exam findings (tenderness over the medial calcaneal tuberosity, pain with toe dorsiflexion) under history findings. Its 'first few steps in the morning' is not in the script, which says the pain is worse in the morning and after prolonged sitting; 'first few steps after sitting' comes from the SP notes.
Gold rank 2 'Diffuse pain over heel' is not supported by the script (pain most intense in the right heel), and 'Refractory to conservative management' rests only on the note's 'limited relief'.
Raw sheet artifact: part of the Foreign body / Ankle sprain rationale text is pasted into the examinee checklist after 'Entrance'. Parsed fields are not affected.
The note exam reports a nonantalgic gait, while the SP is told to show pain with the first few steps after sitting (x018); not necessarily a contradiction.
annotator_notes: p005 and p006 both answer when the pain is worse; merged into one fact (f007).
Training for a marathon (f004, p003) and being a runner (f037, p023) are kept as separate social facts because they say different things.

Note-only facts added (from_note): no proximal radiation (f011), limited relief of conservative measures (f017), PMH denials of cancer, rheumatologic disorders, and diabetes (f029-f031), and family denials of cancer and diabetes (f034-f035).
Daily intermittent heel pain is the ongoing presenting problem, so its attributes are marked current rather than recurrent.

SP-simulated findings: pain on toe extension (x016) and on palpation of the arch and plantar heel (x017) are examination findings; pain with the first few steps after sitting (x018) is added too because it is elicited when the examinee watches him walk (gait/ambulation is part of the checklist exam).
Reviewer edit: environment commentary moved from `finding` to `flags` for x010, x011.
